title: Canonical induced morphism of relative Proj
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme and let $\mathcal A,\mathcal B$ be quasi-coherent graded $\mathcal O_S$-algebras in the affine-basis interface of relative Proj [def-nagata-relative-proj]. Let $q:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ be a degree-preserving $\mathcal O_S$-algebra morphism compatible with affine restriction. Write $\mathcal A(V)_+$ and $\mathcal B(V)_+$ for the ideals generated by the positive-degree elements. Define the irrelevant-ideal condition on $q$ to mean that, for every affine open $V\subset S$, $\mathcal B(V)_+\subseteq q_V(\mathcal A(V)_+)\mathcal B(V)$. Given this condition, define $\operatorname{Proj}_S(q):\operatorname{Proj}_S(\mathcal B)\to\operatorname{Proj}_S(\mathcal A)$ by gluing the affine-base Proj maps. On homogeneous primes the affine map is inverse image under $q_V$; on equal-degree fractions it is induced by $b/f^n\mapsto q_V(b)/q_V(f)^n$. Equivalently its composite with each canonical affine-base chart embedding is $\operatorname{Proj}(q_V)$ followed by the corresponding target chart embedding. This is the specified morphism over $S$, not an arbitrary choice of an arrow.
